strings.name: Frances Arnold
strings.summary: Frances Arnold applies cycles of mutation and selection to engineer enzymes, using evolution in the laboratory to change protein function. Trained first in mechanical and aerospace engineering, she moved into chemical engineering and developed directed evolution at Caltech. The methods help produce catalysts for industry and chemical synthesis. She received half the 2018 Nobel Prize in Chemistry; the work combines evolutionary principles with collaborative experimental design and validation.

strings.highlights.highlight-1.title: Directed evolution of enzymes
strings.highlights.highlight-1.text: Changed enzyme activity and working conditions through repeated variation and selection for desired properties.
strings.highlights.highlight-2.title: Catalysis for synthesis
strings.highlights.highlight-2.text: Advanced engineered enzymes for chemical reactions, connecting basic research, manufacturing and sustainable chemistry.
strings.timeline.event-1.title: Nobel Prize in Chemistry
strings.timeline.event-1.text: Received half the prize for directed evolution of enzymes; George Smith and Gregory Winter shared the other half.
strings.timeline.event-2.title: Millennium Technology Prize
strings.timeline.event-2.text: Recognized for the technological impact of directed evolution and protein engineering.
strings.timeline.event-3.title: Draper Prize
strings.timeline.event-3.text: Recognized for engineering contributions to enzyme evolution, becoming the first woman to receive the prize.
strings.timeline.event-4.title: Enzyme directed-evolution experiment
strings.timeline.event-4.text: Demonstrated that repeated mutation and selection could yield enzymes better suited to chosen conditions.
strings.timeline.event-5.title: Caltech assistant professorship
strings.timeline.event-5.text: Became an assistant professor of chemical engineering after visiting research work and established her group.
strings.timeline.event-6.title: Chemical-engineering doctorate
strings.timeline.event-6.text: Completed her UC Berkeley doctorate before postdoctoral work in biophysical chemistry.
strings.timeline.event-7.title: Princeton engineering degree
strings.timeline.event-7.text: Completed mechanical and aerospace engineering studies and began work on renewable energy.
strings.timeline.event-8.title: Born in East Pittsburgh
strings.timeline.event-8.text: Born in East Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, and grew up around science and engineering.
